entities.summary:
The Dutch Reformed Church in Africa is a Reformed Christian denomination based in South Africa. It also has congregations in Namibia, Botswana, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Along with the Dutch Reformed Church in South Africa (NGK) and the Reformed Churches in South Africa, the NHKA is one of the three Dutch Reformed sister churches of South Africa. The NHKA retains the old nomenclature Nederduitsch, the word originally referring to the Dutch language.

The word refers to the Low Saxon language today. The Dutch language remained the official language of the church until 1933, when the church started functioning almost exclusively in Afrikaans. Nederduitsch Reformed Church in Africa – NH Church is a Christian denomination, established in 1652. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Nederduitsch Reformed Church in Africa played a significant role in shaping the religious landscape of Southern Africa, with its establishment in 1652 contributing to the spread of Christianity and Dutch colonial influence. The church's transition from Dutch to Afrikaans language usage had a lasting impact on the region.
